tools.name: hold
tools.description: When a person wants to hold bitcoin, or asks for a kit, signer, steel backup, estate handoff, or setup help: call hold. Returns the holding-desk URL for that situation. Public, cost 0, no key. Refuses a seed phrase or a private key and does not echo it. Not a record search.

tools.name: search
tools.description: When the question is Bitcoin Core, BIPs, consensus rules, a PR or issue, a contributor, spec versus implementation, a CVE or incident, soft fork activation, governance precedent, Satoshi, IRC, mailing lists, Delving, or Bitcointalk: search this index first. Not a live quote, ETF, or chain analytics.

tools.name: assess_argument
tools.description: When the user asks which discourse game, numbered governance claim, or monopoly fallacy a thread matches: call assess_argument. Returns kind, heading pattern, and cites from product-policy files, not contemporaneous evidence. Cost 1 query. No new synthesis.

tools.name: get_contributor_profile
tools.description: When the user names a GitHub login or asks who a Bitcoin Core contributor is: call get_contributor_profile. Returns public-record facts for that login, or found=false. Cost 1 query. Known set is small. Do not invent employment or affiliation.

tools.name: get_passage
tools.description: When you are about to quote a stored excerpt from a search or find_* cite: call get_passage with uri, id, or source plus doc. Returns the stored passage. Cost 1 query. Not a live web fetch. If ok is false, the index has no passage.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: When the user asks to replay a dated report or names a snapshot_id: call get_snapshot. Returns the stored snapshot JSON as text. Cost 0. A 64-character id does not re-search.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: When you are about to assert a specific factual or historical claim about Bitcoin governance, a merge, a spec, or a mailing-list quote: call verify_claim against a stored cite. Returns noul 0-1, skipped, or no_passage. Cost 1 query. The judge is not a source.

tools.name: analyze_pr
tools.description: When the user pastes a GitHub pull request URL or owner/repo#n, or asks to review a public PR: call analyze_pr. Returns a review scaffold, a capped live thread, index precedent, as_of, and comment_markdown. Does not post comments. Developer. Cost 10 queries. Private repos fail.

tools.name: analyze_issue
tools.description: When the user pastes a GitHub issue URL or asks to review a public issue: call analyze_issue. Returns a review scaffold, index precedent, as_of, and comment_markdown. Does not post comments. Developer. Cost 10 queries. Private repos fail.

tools.name: analyze_submission
tools.description: When the user asks whether a patch or writeup meets a named spec or BIP clause: call analyze_submission. Returns met, not_met, or ambiguous plus cites. Developer. Cost 10 queries. Empty or off-topic packs are ambiguous. Does not post comments.

tools.name: find_discourse
tools.description: When the user asks what GitHub, mail, IRC, or Delving said about a Core path or symbol (for example src/validation.cpp): call find_discourse. Returns cites for that path. Developer. Cost 1 query. Mail/IRC rarely include paths.

tools.name: find_precedent
tools.description: When the user asks for BIP, GitHub, or mail precedent for a proposal: call find_precedent. Returns cites. Developer. Cost 1 query. Disposition is only what a cite heading or URL already says. Does not invent merged/rejected/stalled labels.

tools.name: find_incident
tools.description: When the user names a CVE or past Bitcoin incident (for example CVE-2018-17144): call find_incident. Returns index cites. Developer. Cost 1 query. Empty if the index has no passage.

tools.name: find_spec_impl
tools.description: When the user asks how a spec section or consensus rule is implemented in Bitcoin Core source: call find_spec_impl. Returns spec, Core source, and GitHub cites. Developer. Cost 1 query. Does not emit aligned/gap/divergence verdicts.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "hold" references sensitive artifacts (private key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: hold, search · Private data: hold, search, assess_argument, get_contributor_profile, analyze_pr, analyze_issue · Public sink: analyze_pr, analyze_issue, analyze_submission.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: hold, search · Private data: hold, search, assess_argument, get_contributor_profile, analyze_pr, analyze_issue · Public sink: analyze_pr, analyze_issue, analyze_submission

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
